title: Crews and roles
scope: The flightcrew roster, what each role guarantees, and where crew files live. Excludes the pilot's own teams (see teams-and-dispatch).

statements.statement: "FlightCrew" is literally a bunch of agents working together to complete a (flight) mission, so they are important too.
statements.context: Correcting an assumption that the interfaces mattered more than the crew.

statements.statement: chained internal agent context. spec-builder receives and idea, test-builder receives a spec, orchestrator receives spec, tests and kickoff.
statements.context: Describing how context was meant to travel between roles.

statements.statement: I think not having an interface builderand a backup scribe is a problem.
statements.context: Reviewing the roster the first build run produced.

statements.statement: The test builder is probably an interactive session. particulary if you build tests before anything else. also often needs back and forth between spec and tests.
statements.context: Same turn, on which roles cannot be fire-and-forget.

statements.statement: interface-builder: writes wave-zero seams and halts on a spec–codebase contradiction instead of iterating to green | strong-worker: one retry of a red unit on a stronger tier from a clean state before a human is asked | per-unit adversary: attacks a completed unit before merge for what its checks missed | scribe: assembles the report and log entry and notices when assembly fails
statements.context: Choosing which new roles the rebuild should add.

statements.statement: a role's own guarantees (worker check-after-edit, read-only roles' write denial) are declared in its frontmatter hooks; global hooks keep only what applies to every role.
statements.context: Agreeing that role guarantees belong in the role file rather than in global hooks.

statements.statement: crew/ is the source of truth for flightcrew agents. FLIGHTLOG goes into the bootstrap, RUNLOG stays where they are. remove any other redundant files.
statements.context: Settling where the crew files live and what else can be deleted.

statements.statement: you are a key member of the flightcrew line up and have already been constrained by the systems requirements
statements.context: Reminding the spec builder that it is itself part of the system it is specifying.
